purpose: Acquire a small provenance-controlled nature corpus and test whether biological and ecological mechanisms can be translated into bounded engineering hypotheses.
rights_boundary: Project Gutenberg source pages identify these texts as public domain in the USA. The workflow downloads source text only for transient verification and records metadata, hashes, statistics and bounded derived hypotheses. It does not commit or redistribute the full texts.

sources.title: The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection
sources.author: Charles Darwin
mechanism_hypotheses: environmental pressure filters alternatives over repeated cycles
branching preserves diversity while enabling specialization

sources.title: Walden, and On The Duty Of Civil Disobedience
sources.author: Henry David Thoreau
mechanism_hypotheses: deliberate constraints reduce waste and reveal essential function
direct observation produces stronger feedback than inherited assumption
simplicity can increase resilience by lowering dependency load
periodic withdrawal creates space for system-level reflection

sources.title: The Life of the Bee
sources.author: Maurice Maeterlinck
mechanism_hypotheses: distributed coordination can emerge from local role rules
specialization raises throughput but requires shared survival signals
redundancy and replacement protect collective continuity
collective adaptation may outperform isolated optimization

promotion_boundary.GERMINATED: At least one authorised source must be fetched by an external workflow, validated, hashed and durably read back with passing tests.
promotion_boundary.ROOTED: The corpus and translation runtime must repeat successfully with durable monitoring, maintenance and recovery evidence.
promotion_boundary.SPROUT: At least one mechanism hypothesis must produce a useful tested capability or design improvement with independent proof.
